commitments.quote: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as permitted by this BAA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use and disclose PHI only to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as this BAA permits.
commitments.scope: PHI (HIPAA definition, including limited data sets under 2.4) created, received, maintained or transmitted for Example Health System and its affiliated hospitals and clinics under any Underlying Agreement.
commitments.deviation: The DPA ties processing to Customer's documented instructions, including Customer's configuration of the Services. The BAA instead limits use to performing the Underlying Agreements, uses required by law, and uses the BAA permits.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.scope: All uses and disclosures of PHI.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may de-identify PHI only by the HIPAA safe harbor method and may use the resulting data only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.scope: De-identification of PHI and any use of the de-identified output.
commitments.deviation: The DPA lets ExampleCo use Usage Data (aggregated or de-identified data) to operate, secure and improve the Services, with no prescribed de-identification method. The BAA requires the safe harbor method and limits use to providing and improving the services under the Underlying Agreements. The BAA does not address model training. Inference: model training on de-identified data would be permitted only if it serves to provide or improve those services.

commitments.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
commitments.summary: Data de-identified under the safe harbor method falls outside PHI and outside the BAA.
commitments.scope: Only data de-identified by the safe harbor method in Section 2.3 is excluded. Data de-identified by other methods (for example, expert determination) is not excluded by this sentence and, inferentially, remains PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA's Usage Data carve-out covers any aggregated or de-identified data that does not identify Customer or a person, by any method. The BAA's carve-out is limited to safe harbor de-identification. Note that the 2.3 use restriction is stated alongside the carve-out, although the de-identified data otherwise falls outside the BAA.

commitments.quote: A limited data set under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) is PHI for all purposes of this BAA.
commitments.summary: Limited data sets are treated as PHI for every purpose under the BAA.
commitments.scope: Limited data sets under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) are brought fully within PHI. They therefore trigger the use limits, the US-only rule, breach reporting and return or destruction.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. Inference: under the DPA, such data would likely be Personal Data anyway, but the DPA has no express rule on partially de-identified data.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to ePHI.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule for ePHI.
commitments.scope: ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires ExampleCo's own Security Measures in Annex 2 and lets ExampleCo update them unilaterally if overall security is not materially reduced. The BAA imposes the HIPAA Security Rule as the standard and contains no unilateral update right.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not store or process PHI outside the United States.
commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets. Under 5.1, the same restriction flows down to Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: The DPA stores data at rest in whatever hosting region Customer selects. The BAA mandates the United States only, and it covers processing as well as storage.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not access PHI from outside the United States, which bars offshore support access.
commitments.scope: Access to any PHI by ExampleCo personnel and, through the 5.1 flow-down, by Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: The DPA expressly permits access from outside the hosting region, including from the Manila, Philippines support center, under SCCs. The BAA prohibits any non-US access, so the Manila support model cannot touch PHI.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.scope: Systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits to SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001, or substantially equivalent successors. The BAA requires HITRUST r2 specifically, which is not among the DPA certifications, and gives no successor-standard substitution.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and no later than 10 calendar days after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery of the Breach. Under the HIPAA definition incorporated by 1.1 (45 C.F.R. § 164.410(a)(2)), this is the first day the Breach is known to ExampleCo, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known, to any ExampleCo workforce member or agent other than the person committing it.

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example, in writing, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example (per 4.4).
commitments.scope: Breaches of Unsecured PHI as defined by HIPAA, in any form, including paper or oral. No precedence term ranks this against 4.2. Where a Breach also involves a Security Incident affecting ePHI, the 4.2 five-business-day report would also apply and fall due first.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires notice within 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a breach. The BAA allows longer (10 calendar days), but its clock starts earlier: at Discovery, including constructive knowledge of any workforce member or agent, rather than at ExampleCo's confirmation.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any Security Incident within 5 business days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo becoming aware of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example, in writing, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example (per 4.4).
commitments.scope: Security Incidents under 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, which include attempted as well as successful unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification or destruction, or interference with systems. They are limited to incidents involving ePHI that ExampleCo or its Subcontractors handle for Covered Entity. Unsuccessful attempts are covered by the standing notice in the second sentence of 4.2.
commitments.deviation: The DPA notifies only confirmed Personal Data Breaches, within 72 hours of confirmation, and excludes unsuccessful attempts. The BAA requires reports of all Security Incidents involving ePHI, including successful incidents that are not confirmed breaches. Its period is 5 business days from awareness rather than from confirmation.

commitments.quote: This Section 4.2 serves as notice of, and no further report is required for, unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.summary: The BAA itself serves as standing notice of unsuccessful attempts, such as pings, port scans and blocked log-ins, so no individual reports are needed for them.
commitments.scope: Unsuccessful attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA excludes unsuccessful attempts (including denial-of-service attacks) from the breach definition altogether. The BAA treats them as Security Incidents but deems notice given. Its examples do not list denial-of-service. Inference: a denial-of-service attack interfering with system operations could be a reportable Security Incident.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any use or disclosure of PHI that the BAA does not permit within 10 calendar days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo becoming aware of the impermissible use or disclosure

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example, in writing, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example (per 4.4).
commitments.scope: Any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by the BAA, whether or not it is a Breach or a Security Incident. Examples include non-minimum-necessary uses and non-US access.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no separate duty to report impermissible uses. It notifies only confirmed Personal Data Breaches, within 72 hours of confirmation.

commitments.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example.
commitments.summary: All Section 4 reports must be in writing to the Privacy Office, with a copy to the Information Security Office.
commitments.recipient: Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example; copy to Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example.
commitments.scope: All reports under 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the security contact designated in the admin console, or failing that the account owner. The BAA fixes two named email addresses and requires a written report, so ExampleCo's default console-contact routing would not satisfy it.

commitments.quote: A report of a Breach shall include, to the extent known, the identity of each individual affected, the PHI involved, the date of the Breach and of its Discovery, and the steps taken to mitigate it.
commitments.summary: Breach reports must include, to the extent known, each affected individual's identity, the PHI involved, the Breach and Discovery dates, and mitigation steps.
commitments.recipient: Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example; copy to iso@ehs.example.
commitments.scope: Reports of Breaches of Unsecured PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA's notice covers the nature of the breach, data categories and measures taken, and promises further information as it becomes available. The BAA requires individual-level identification and specific dates. It has no express duty to supplement later, although 'to the extent known' leaves updates implicit (inference).

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must reimburse Example Health System's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors.
commitments.scope: Breaches caused by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors. Covered costs are notification costs to individuals, regulators and the media.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA (7.4) states that breach notification is not an acknowledgment of fault, and the BAA has no comparable disclaimer.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must ensure each Subcontractor handling PHI agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions as ExampleCo, including the US-only rule.
commitments.scope: Subcontractors under 45 C.F.R. § 160.103 that create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI, which would include AI model providers handling PHI (inference).
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes ExampleCo responsible for its Subprocessors' performance and pairs this with a general authorization, 30-day notice and an objection right. The BAA requires a written flow-down of identical terms, including no non-US access, and is silent on notice of or objection to new Subcontractors.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within ten (10) business days after Covered Entity's request, so Covered Entity can meet 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Example Health System within 10 business days after its request.

deadline.anchor: Covered Entity's request

commitments.scope: PHI in a Designated Record Set, to support individual access rights under 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the HHS Secretary for HIPAA compliance review.
commitments.recipient: Secretary of Health and Human Services
commitments.scope: Internal practices, books and records relating to PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits audits to Trust Center reports, plus one on-site audit per 12 months with 60 days' notice when a supervisory authority requires it, at Customer's expense. The BAA grants the regulator access with no frequency, notice or cost limits.

commitments.quote: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI within thirty (30) days.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must return or destroy all PHI within 30 days after the Underlying Agreements terminate.

deadline.anchor: termination of the Underlying Agreements

commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets and, inferentially, backups. Safe-harbor de-identified data is excluded.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows 90 days to delete, plus a further 35 days for backups to be overwritten, and offers no return option. The BAA requires return or destruction of all PHI within 30 days, with no separate backup allowance. The BAA has no counterpart to the DPA 10.2 deletion certification.

commitments.quote: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.summary: Where return or destruction is not feasible, ExampleCo must keep applying the BAA's protections to any PHI it retains for as long as it keeps it.
commitments.scope: PHI that cannot feasibly be returned or destroyed. Inference: this could include backups that are not overwritten within 30 days.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier.
commitments.summary: The Addendum overrides any conflicting term in the Agreement, order forms, and any Supplier DPA or policy, including the ExampleCo standard DPA.
commitments.scope: All conflicts between this Addendum and the Agreement, order forms, or any Supplier-provided DPA, privacy policy or other document; most significantly displaces the DPA's 72-hour confirmed-breach notice standard.
commitments.deviation: The DPA says the DPA controls over the Agreement for processing of personal data. Here the Bank Addendum controls over the Supplier DPA itself, so the DPA's terms yield wherever they conflict.

commitments.quote: Terms incorporated by reference to a Supplier website, including any Supplier trust or security site, do not bind Bank and do not modify this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Terms on Supplier websites, including the Trust Center, do not bind Bank or modify the Addendum.
commitments.scope: Any Supplier website terms, including Trust Center subprocessor lists, NDA terms and published reports.
commitments.deviation: The DPA relies on the Trust Center for the subprocessor list, subprocessor notices, report access under NDA terms, and AI model provider listings. None of these bind Bank.

commitments.quote: "Bank Data" means all data and information, in any form, that Supplier or any Subcontractor receives, accesses, creates or processes in connection with the Agreement, including (a) data provided by or on behalf of Bank or its customers; (b) metadata, logs and configuration data relating to Bank's use of the Services; and (c) any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized.
commitments.summary: Protected Bank Data covers all data in any form, including metadata, logs, model outputs, embeddings, and aggregated or de-identified derivatives.
commitments.scope: All data, not only personal data. This includes metadata, logs, configuration data, and derived data such as model outputs, embeddings, annotations and aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA covers only Customer Personal Data and carves out aggregated or de-identified Usage Data that Supplier may use under 8.2. Here that data remains Bank Data, so the Usage Data carve-out has no room to operate.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a written information security program that is consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the FFIEC Information Technology Examination Handbook.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep a written security program consistent with the NIST CSF and the FFIEC IT Examination Handbook.
commitments.deviation: The DPA refers to Annex 2 measures and lets Supplier update them unilaterally. Here Supplier must follow specific frameworks (NIST CSF, FFIEC), and the Addendum contains no unilateral update right.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data at rest using AES-256 or stronger and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Bank Data must be encrypted at rest with AES-256 or stronger and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, including derived data and metadata.
commitments.deviation: The encryption standards are substantively the same. The obligation applies to the broader Bank Data definition and cannot be changed by Supplier updates.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.summary: MFA is required for all remote access to systems handling Bank Data.
commitments.scope: All remote access to any system that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires MFA for access to production systems. Here MFA is required for all remote access to any system that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall complete a criminal background check on all Supplier Personnel before granting them access to Bank Data, to the extent permitted by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier must background-check all Supplier and Subcontractor personnel before giving them access to Bank Data, where the law allows.
commitments.scope: Supplier Personnel, meaning employees, contractors and agents of Supplier and of any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires only confidentiality obligations for personnel. Criminal background checks are an added requirement.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain throughout the term of the Agreement a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services for the whole term.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires both SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, or substantially equivalent successor standards. This Addendum requires a current SOC 2 Type II only, with no successor-standard substitution and no ISO 27001 requirement.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall store and process Bank Data only within the United States.
commitments.summary: All storage and processing of Bank Data must stay in the United States.
commitments.scope: Both storage and processing of all Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA fixes only the at-rest storage region chosen by the customer. Here both storage and processing must be in the US.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any Supplier Personnel located outside the United States to access Bank Data, including for support or maintenance, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.summary: No personnel outside the US may access Bank Data, even for support or maintenance, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.scope: All Supplier and Subcontractor personnel outside the US, including support and maintenance staff.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows offshore access for support, maintenance and security, including from the Manila support center. Here such access is prohibited without Bank's prior written approval.

commitments.quote: Supplier may permit only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 ("Approved Subcontractors") to access Bank Data, and each only within the scope stated for it in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: Only the Schedule 2 subcontractors may access Bank Data, and each only within its stated scope.
commitments.scope: Subcontractors include Supplier Affiliates and any third party with access to Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA grants general authorization based on a Trust Center list. Here authorization is a closed list in Schedule 2, and each subcontractor is limited to its stated scope.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, delivered as provided in Exhibit C, before adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.summary: Supplier must give 90 days' prior written notice to Bank's TPRM office before adding, replacing or expanding the scope of a subcontractor.

deadline.anchor: adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope

commitments.recipient: Third-Party Risk Management office, tprm-notices@enb.example, with a copy to Example National Bank, N.A., Legal Department, 100 Example Plaza, New York, NY 10001
commitments.scope: New or replacement subcontractors and expansions of an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.deviation: The notice period rises from 30 to 90 days. Notice must be written and delivered to the TPRM office with a copy to Legal, rather than posted on the Trust Center or emailed to subscribers. Scope expansions also trigger notice. The Addendum contains no emergency-replacement exception like DPA 5.4.

commitments.quote: Bank may object within thirty (30) days after receiving the notice. If Bank objects, Supplier shall not engage the Subcontractor for the Services provided to Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
commitments.summary: Bank may object within 30 days; if it does, Supplier may not use the subcontractor for Bank, or Bank may terminate without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund.

deadline.anchor: Bank's receipt of the subcontractor notice

commitments.deviation: The objection window is 30 days rather than 15, and Bank need not state data protection grounds. On objection, Supplier may not engage the subcontractor for Bank. The termination right carries no penalty and comes with a pro-rata refund, and it is not a sole remedy.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall impose on each Subcontractor written obligations at least as protective of Bank Data as this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Supplier must flow down written obligations at least as protective as this Addendum to every subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six (6) hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must contractually require each subcontractor to report Security Incidents to Supplier within 6 hours of the subcontractor's Discovery.

deadline.anchor: the Subcontractor's Discovery: the earliest time the Subcontractor knew, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident

commitments.scope: Actual or reasonably suspected Security Incidents.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier remains fully liable to Bank for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Supplier is fully liable for its subcontractors' acts and omissions.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes Supplier responsible only for subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations. Here Supplier is fully liable for all of their acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: Amazon Web Services, Inc. | Infrastructure hosting | All Bank Data, US regions only | United States
commitments.summary: AWS may host all Bank Data, in US regions only.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, US regions only.
commitments.deviation: The approval is a fixed contractual listing with a location restriction, rather than an entry on the Trust Center list.

commitments.quote: Model Provider A, Inc. | Large-model inference for AI agent features | Prompts and outputs only; zero retention | United States
commitments.summary: Model Provider A may receive only prompts and outputs for inference, with zero retention, in the US.
commitments.scope: Prompts and outputs only.
commitments.deviation: Zero retention applies with no abuse-monitoring exception, and processing is US-only.

commitments.quote: Labelforge, Inc. | Human annotation of feedback samples | Only de-identified feedback samples that Bank submits through the Services' feedback feature, for improving Bank's own agents. Bank Data in identifiable form is not permitted. | United States; US-based annotators only
commitments.summary: Labelforge may annotate only de-identified feedback samples that Bank submits, only to improve Bank's own agents, using US-based annotators.
commitments.scope: De-identified feedback samples submitted by Bank through the feedback feature. These remain Bank Data under Section 2.2.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. | Support ticketing | Contact details of Bank users only | United States
commitments.summary: Helpdesk Platform may process only Bank users' contact details, for support ticketing, in the US.
commitments.scope: Contact details of Bank users only.
commitments.deviation: The approval is a fixed contractual listing with data-category and location limits.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and no later than 12 hours after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery: the earliest time at which Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center, by telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147 and by email cfc-thirdparty@enb.example
commitments.scope: Any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration or destruction of, Bank Data. Also any unauthorized access to a Supplier or Subcontractor system handling Bank Data, whether or not access to Bank Data is confirmed.
commitments.deviation: The deadline is 12 hours, not 72. The clock starts at actual or constructive knowledge by Supplier or any Subcontractor, not at Supplier's confirmation. Suspected incidents and system intrusions count, and the DPA's exclusions for unsuccessful attempts do not apply.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C. Notice provided only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must go by both telephone and email to the Cyber Fusion Center; notice only to the relationship manager or via a status page or trust site does not count.
commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center, telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147 and email cfc-thirdparty@enb.example (not relationship manager Dana Okafor, dana.okafor@enb.example, who handles routine matters only)
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the console-designated security contact or the account owner. Here notice must go by both phone and email to the Cyber Fusion Center at fixed contact details. Relationship manager, status page and trust site notice are expressly insufficient.

commitments.quote: Supplier's initial notice shall include all information then known about the Security Incident, including the date and time of Discovery, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
commitments.summary: The initial notice must include all known information, including the time of Discovery, the systems and subcontractors involved, and the affected data categories.
commitments.deviation: The required content is broader: all information then known, the Discovery date and time, the systems and subcontractors involved, and data potentially affected.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall provide written status updates at least once every twenty-four (24) hours until the Security Incident is contained
commitments.summary: Supplier must send written status updates at least every 24 hours until containment.

deadline.anchor: from the initial notice until the Security Incident is contained

commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center (inference: the contract does not separately specify where updates go)
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires further information only as it becomes available. Here Supplier must send fixed 24-hour written updates.

commitments.quote: and shall deliver a written root-cause report within thirty (30) days after containment.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment.

deadline.anchor: containment of the Security Incident

commitments.deviation: The DPA has no root-cause report requirement.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not notify any Bank customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media of a Security Incident involving Bank Data without Bank's prior written consent, unless required by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not tell Bank customers, regulators, law enforcement or media about an incident without Bank's prior written consent, unless the law requires it.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Where law requires such notice, Supplier shall inform Bank before giving it, to the extent legally permitted.
commitments.summary: Where a legally required external notice must be given, Supplier must tell Bank first, where legally permitted.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall preserve all logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident for at least one (1) year after containment, and shall give Bank and its designated forensic investigator access to that evidence on request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep incident forensic evidence for at least one year after containment and give Bank and its forensic investigator access on request.

deadline.anchor: containment of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Bank and its designated forensic investigator
commitments.scope: Logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall reimburse Bank's reasonable costs of investigating and responding to a Security Incident caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor, including costs of notifying affected individuals and providing them with twenty-four (24) months of credit monitoring.
commitments.summary: Supplier must reimburse Bank's reasonable costs of investigating and responding to incidents caused by Supplier or subcontractors, including individual notification and 24 months of credit monitoring.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA 7.4 says notification is not an acknowledgment of fault, and it contains no cost reimbursement.

commitments.quote: Supplier's obligations to ENB Securities LLC are supplemented by Exhibit D.
commitments.summary: Exhibit D adds to Supplier's obligations toward ENB Securities LLC.
commitments.scope: ENB Securities LLC customer information.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Where this Addendum, the Agreement, any exhibit or schedule, or applicable law specifies more than one period for the same notice, the shortest period applies.
commitments.summary: Where more than one notice period applies to the same notice, the shortest controls, so the 12-hour period in 6.1 governs over Exhibit D's 72 hours.
commitments.scope: All notice periods in the Addendum, Agreement, exhibits, schedules and applicable law.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any artificial intelligence or machine learning model, other than a model used solely to provide the Services to Bank.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any AI/ML model except one used solely to serve Bank.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, including aggregated, de-identified, derived data, outputs and embeddings.
commitments.deviation: The DPA bars only training or fine-tuning foundation models offered to other customers, and 8.2 permits use of Usage Data to improve the Services. Here the bar covers any model and also evaluation and improvement. Derived and de-identified data count as Bank Data, so the Usage Data improvement right is effectively displaced.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any person to review, label or annotate Bank Data for the purpose of developing or improving any model, except as expressly permitted for an Approved Subcontractor in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: No one may review, label or annotate Bank Data for model development except as Schedule 2 permits, which currently means Labelforge's de-identified feedback samples.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall identify in Schedule 2 every third-party model provider that receives Bank Data
commitments.summary: Every third-party model provider receiving Bank Data must be listed in Schedule 2.
commitments.deviation: Model providers must be listed in the contractual Schedule 2 rather than on the Trust Center.

commitments.quote: and shall ensure that no model provider retains Bank Data after returning a response.
commitments.summary: Supplier must ensure that no model provider retains Bank Data after returning a response.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows retention for abuse monitoring and only requires Supplier to impose the terms on providers. Here retention is absolute zero with no exception, and Supplier must ensure it.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least once every twelve (12) months, and shall deliver an executive summary of the results to Bank within thirty (30) days after Bank's request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must have an independent penetration test at least every 12 months and deliver the executive summary within 30 days of Bank's request.

deadline.anchor: each penetration test

secondary_deadline.anchor: Bank's request for the executive summary

commitments.deviation: The summary must be delivered directly to Bank within 30 days of a request, rather than made available on the Trust Center.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall remediate vulnerabilities rated Critical within fifteen (15) days, and vulnerabilities rated High within thirty (30) days, after identification.
commitments.summary: Supplier must fix Critical vulnerabilities within 15 days and High vulnerabilities within 30 days of identification.

deadline.anchor: identification of a Critical vulnerability

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall deliver its SOC 2 Type II report to Bank within thirty (30) days after the report is issued, and a bridge letter on request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver each SOC 2 Type II report within 30 days after issuance, and a bridge letter on request.

deadline.anchor: issuance of the SOC 2 Type II report

commitments.deviation: The report must be delivered directly within 30 days of issuance rather than made available on the Trust Center, and Trust Center NDA acceptance is not a condition. The bridge letter is an added requirement.

commitments.quote: Bank, its auditors and its regulators may audit Supplier's compliance with this Addendum once in any twelve (12) month period on thirty (30) days' written notice
commitments.summary: Bank, its auditors and its regulators may audit Supplier once per 12 months on 30 days' written notice.

deadline.anchor: the audit (Bank's written notice)

commitments.scope: Compliance with this Addendum.
commitments.deviation: The DPA treats reports as satisfying audit rights and allows an on-site audit only if a supervisory authority requires it, on 60 days' notice and at Customer's expense. Here the audit right is unconditional, on 30 days' notice, and extends to auditors and regulators. The Addendum does not state who bears the expense.

commitments.quote: and at any time after a Security Incident on five (5) business days' written notice.
commitments.summary: After any Security Incident, Bank may audit on 5 business days' written notice, outside the annual limit.

deadline.anchor: the post-incident audit (Bank's written notice)

commitments.scope: Audits following any Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no post-incident audit right.

commitments.quote: Nothing in this Addendum limits the access of any regulator with authority over Bank.
commitments.summary: The Addendum places no limits on regulator access.
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits audits to one per 12 months, conditioned on a supervisory authority requirement. Here regulator access is unlimited.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan for the Services with a recovery time objective of no more than four (4) hours and a recovery point objective of no more than one (1) hour.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain a BC/DR plan with an RTO of 4 hours or less and an RPO of 1 hour or less.

deadline.anchor: a disruption of the Services (recovery time objective)

secondary_deadline.anchor: a disruption of the Services (maximum data-loss window, recovery point objective)

commitments.deviation: The DPA requires a BC/DR plan but sets no recovery time or recovery point objectives.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall test the plan at least annually, provide Bank a summary of the results
commitments.summary: Supplier must test the BC/DR plan at least annually and give Bank a summary of the results.

deadline.anchor: each BC/DR plan test

commitments.deviation: Annual testing is the same as the DPA. Supplier must also provide Bank a summary of results.

commitments.quote: and participate in Bank's annual operational resilience exercise on sixty (60) days' written notice.
commitments.summary: Supplier must take part in Bank's annual resilience exercise when given 60 days' written notice.

deadline.anchor: Bank's annual operational resilience exercise (Bank's written notice)

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.summary: Supplier must return Bank Data in Bank's reasonably requested format within 30 days after termination or Bank's written request.

commitments.deviation: The DPA has no return obligation.

deadline.anchor: termination of the Agreement or Bank's written request

commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver an officer-signed certificate of destruction within 10 business days after destruction.

commitments.deviation: The certificate is automatic rather than on request, must be signed by an officer, and is due within a fixed 10 business days.

commitments.summary: The incident, insurance and return/destruction sections survive termination for as long as Supplier or any subcontractor holds Bank Data.

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.summary: Exhibit D adds to Section 6 and does not replace it, so the 12-hour notice and other Section 6 duties still apply to ENB Securities.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: This VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and over any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates.
commitments.summary: The VDPA overrides the Subscription Agreement and any data processing terms or policies of Vendor or its Affiliates, including Affiliate Subprocessor ExampleCo.
commitments.scope: Covers terms of Vendor and its Affiliates. ExampleCo, Inc. is listed as a Vendor Affiliate in Amendment No. 1 to Appendix B, so ExampleCo's standard DPA is displaced where it conflicts. Examples are its 72-hour post-confirmation breach clock, its Usage Data rights and its 90-day deletion period.
commitments.deviation: DPA 11.1 makes the ExampleCo DPA control over the Agreement for processing. Here the Retailer's VDPA prevails over all vendor and Affiliate terms, so the ExampleCo DPA cannot override the VDPA's 24-hour notice, AI and deletion terms.

commitments.quote: "Retailer Data" means all data that Retailer, its employees or its customers provide to Vendor or that Vendor collects from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces and metrics, and all data derived from any of it.
commitments.summary: Retailer Data covers all provided or collected data, including telemetry, logs, traces, metrics and anything derived from them, whether or not it is personal data.
commitments.scope: All data, not just personal data. Derived, aggregated or de-identified data remains Retailer Data, so every VDPA duty, including the AI training restriction, applies to it.
commitments.deviation: The DPA covers only Customer Personal Data (1.1). It treats aggregated or de-identified Usage Data as outside protection and usable by ExampleCo to improve the Services (8.2). Under the VDPA, derived data and telemetry are Retailer Data with no Usage Data carve-out.

commitments.quote: "Data Incident" means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including while held by a Subprocessor.
commitments.summary: Notifiable incidents include actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access, acquisition, disclosure or loss of any Retailer Data, including at a Subprocessor.
commitments.scope: Covers suspected as well as confirmed incidents, all Retailer Data (not only personal data), and incidents at Subprocessors such as ExampleCo.
commitments.deviation: The DPA's Personal Data Breach requires ExampleCo confirmation, is limited to personal data and excludes unsuccessful attempts. The VDPA covers reasonably suspected incidents involving any Retailer Data, with no confirmation requirement.

commitments.quote: "Subprocessor" means any third party, including any Vendor Affiliate, that processes Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf.
commitments.summary: Vendor Affiliates that process Retailer Data, such as ExampleCo, are Subprocessors subject to VDPA subprocessor controls.
commitments.scope: Includes Vendor Affiliates and covers processing of any Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA definition covers third parties processing Customer Personal Data. The VDPA expressly includes Affiliates and extends to all Retailer Data.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall process Retailer Data only to provide the services described in the Subscription Agreement (the "Services") and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.summary: Vendor may process Retailer Data only to provide the Services and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data, including derived data and telemetry.
commitments.deviation: The DPA treats instructions as set out in the Agreement, DPA and service configuration, and lets ExampleCo use Usage Data to improve the Services. The VDPA limits all use of Retailer Data to providing the Services.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not use Retailer Data to train or improve any ML model unless the model is used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.scope: Any machine learning model and all Retailer Data, including derived data and telemetry. This applies to ExampleCo's AI features via flow-down under 5.3.
commitments.deviation: DPA 8.1 bars only training or fine-tuning foundation models made available to other customers, and 8.2 permits using Usage Data to improve the Services. The VDPA bars training or improving any model except Retailer-dedicated ones, and covers derived data.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.summary: Retailer Data may be stored only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.scope: Storage of all Retailer Data. The clause addresses storage only. It does not expressly address remote access from other countries (inference).
commitments.deviation: The DPA stores data in the customer-selected region and, in 6.2, permits access from outside it, including Manila. The VDPA fixes storage to the US or Canada. It is silent on offshore access, so whether Manila support access is permitted is not expressly resolved (inference).

commitments.quote: Vendor shall maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards that meet or exceed the CIS Critical Security Controls, Implementation Group 2.
commitments.summary: Vendor must maintain safeguards meeting or exceeding CIS Critical Security Controls IG2.
commitments.deviation: The DPA uses its own Annex 2 measures, which ExampleCo may update unilaterally. The VDPA sets an external CIS IG2 benchmark and has no unilateral update right.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.summary: Vendor must encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit with industry-standard encryption.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA specifies AES-256 and TLS 1.2+. The VDPA requires industry-standard encryption without naming algorithms.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall obtain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services each year
commitments.summary: Vendor must obtain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services every year.

deadline.anchor: each year

commitments.deviation: The DPA requires SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, or substantially equivalent successors. The VDPA requires an annual SOC 2 Type II only, with no ISO 27001 requirement and no successor-standard substitution.

commitments.quote: provide it to Retailer within fifteen (15) days after Retailer's request.
commitments.summary: Vendor must deliver the SOC 2 Type II report to Retailer within 15 days after request.

deadline.anchor: Retailer's request

commitments.deviation: The DPA makes the report available through the Trust Center, subject to NDA terms. The VDPA requires direct delivery within 15 days, with no NDA condition.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
commitments.summary: Only Appendix B Subprocessors may process Retailer Data unless Retailer gives prior written consent.
commitments.scope: Appendix B lists AWS (hosting, US), Helpdesk Platform (support ticketing, US) and, by Amendment No. 1, ExampleCo (platform hosting and AI features, US).
commitments.deviation: The DPA grants general authorization with a Trust Center list. The VDPA requires specific prior written consent for any Subprocessor not in Appendix B.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall request consent for a new Subprocessor in writing at least thirty (30) days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data.
commitments.summary: Vendor must request written consent at least 30 days before a new Subprocessor begins processing.

deadline.anchor: new Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data

commitments.recipient: Retailer (written request; no specific contact given)
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives 30 days' notice by Trust Center update and email to subscribers. The VDPA requires a direct written consent request. It has no urgent-replacement exception like DPA 5.4.

commitments.quote: Retailer's silence is not consent.
commitments.summary: A new Subprocessor is not approved unless Retailer affirmatively consents.
commitments.deviation: Under the DPA, the customer must object within 15 days, and its sole remedy is termination. Under the VDPA, silence is not consent and no deemed approval occurs.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA
commitments.summary: Vendor must contractually flow down obligations at least as protective as the VDPA to every Subprocessor, including ExampleCo.
commitments.scope: All Subprocessors, including Affiliates such as ExampleCo.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: and remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
commitments.summary: Vendor remains liable for all acts and omissions of its Subprocessors.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations. The VDPA imposes liability for all Subprocessor acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo, Inc. (Vendor Affiliate) | Platform hosting and AI features for the Services | United States
commitments.summary: ExampleCo, a Vendor Affiliate, was approved on September 8, 2025 as a Subprocessor for platform hosting and AI features, located in the United States.
commitments.scope: ExampleCo's processing is limited to platform hosting and AI features for the Services, in the United States, and is subject to the VDPA via 1.1 and 5.3.
commitments.deviation: ExampleCo's standard DPA would allow notice 72 hours after confirmation, Usage Data use, Manila support access and 90-day deletion. The VDPA prevails over Affiliate terms (1.1) and requires flow-down (5.3). Its US location fits VDPA 3.3, but the VDPA does not expressly bar ExampleCo's offshore access under DPA 6.2 (inference).

commitments.quote: Vendor shall notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: Vendor must notify Retailer of any Data Incident without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Vendor (XYZwire) becomes aware of an actual or reasonably suspected Data Incident, including one at a Subprocessor; no confirmation required

commitments.recipient: Retailer Security Operations: email secops@erg.example and telephone +1 (614) 555-0182
commitments.scope: Actual or reasonably suspected incidents involving any Retailer Data, including at Subprocessors such as ExampleCo. The clause keys to Vendor's awareness. Whether a Subprocessor's awareness is imputed is not stated (inference), though 5.3 flow-down requires equally protective Subprocessor terms.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach. The VDPA requires 24 hours from awareness of a suspected or actual incident. Under 1.1, the VDPA period controls over ExampleCo's terms.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall send notice by email to Retailer Security Operations at secops@erg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182. Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must go by both email and phone to Retailer Security Operations; notice to account or procurement contacts does not count.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the console-designated security contact or, failing that, the account owner. The VDPA fixes specific email and phone channels and excludes account contacts.

commitments.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken.
commitments.summary: The incident notice must describe the incident, the affected Retailer Data, any Subprocessor involved and the steps taken.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires content only to the extent then known and does not require identifying Subprocessors. The VDPA requires identification of any Subprocessor involved.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall supplement the notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.summary: Vendor must update the incident notice as new information emerges.
commitments.deviation: Substantially similar to the DPA's further-information commitment.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, except as required by law.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not disclose a Data Incident to Retailer's customers or third parties without Retailer's prior written approval, unless required by law.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall cooperate with Retailer's investigation
commitments.summary: Vendor must cooperate with Retailer's investigation of a Data Incident.

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. DPA 7.4 states that notification is not an acknowledgment of fault, and the DPA has no cost-bearing duty.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after the Subscription Agreement ends, Vendor shall delete all Retailer Data
commitments.summary: Vendor must delete all Retailer Data within 30 days after the Subscription Agreement ends.

commitments.summary: Vendor must confirm deletion to Retailer in writing.

commitments.deviation: The DPA certifies deletion only on written request. The VDPA requires written confirmation automatically.

commitments.summary: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance once per calendar year on 30 days' notice.

commitments.recipient: Security contact designated in the Services administration console, or Customer's account owner
commitments.scope: Personal Data Breach

commitments.quote: ExampleCo's notification of or response to a Personal Data Breach is not an acknowledgment of fault or liability.
commitments.summary: Notifying or responding to a breach does not mean ExampleCo admits fault or liability.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune any foundation model that is made available to other customers.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune foundation models that are made available to other customers.
commitments.scope: Customer Data in general, not only Customer Personal Data. Inference: training models that are not offered to other customers is not prohibited.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.
commitments.scope: Usage Data: aggregated or de-identified data that does not identify Customer or any natural person

commitments.quote: ExampleCo lists the third-party model providers used by AI features as Subprocessors on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo lists the third-party AI model providers as Subprocessors on the Trust Center.
commitments.scope: Third-party model providers used by AI features

commitments.quote: ExampleCo requires its model providers not to retain prompts or outputs beyond the time needed to return a response, except as required for abuse monitoring.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo requires its model providers to keep prompts and outputs only as long as needed to return a response, except where needed for abuse monitoring.
commitments.scope: Prompts and outputs sent to third-party model providers

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will make its most recent SOC 2 Type II report available to Customer through the Trust Center, subject to Customer's acceptance of the Trust Center non-disclosure terms.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make its latest SOC 2 Type II report available through the Trust Center once Customer accepts the Trust Center non-disclosure terms.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least annually and will make an executive summary of the results available through the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must have an independent third party penetration-test the Services at least once a year and post an executive summary of the results on the Trust Center.

deadline.anchor: Annual penetration test

commitments.scope: The Services

commitments.quote: Customer agrees that the reports in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 satisfy any audit right under Data Protection Laws.
commitments.summary: Customer agrees that the SOC 2 report and the penetration test summary satisfy its statutory audit rights.

commitments.quote: Where a supervisory authority requires a further audit, Customer may conduct one on-site audit per twelve (12) month period, with at least sixty (60) days' written notice, during business hours, and at Customer's expense.
commitments.summary: Where a supervisory authority requires it, Customer may conduct one on-site audit every 12 months, with at least 60 days' written notice, during business hours and at its own expense.

deadline.anchor: On-site audit

secondary_deadline.anchor: Limit of one on-site audit per 12-month period

commitments.scope: Only where a supervisory authority requires a further audit

commitments.quote: Within ninety (90) days after termination or expiry of the Agreement, ExampleCo will delete Customer Personal Data from the Services. Backups are overwritten in the ordinary course within a further thirty-five (35) days.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must delete Customer Personal Data from the Services within 90 days after the Agreement ends, and backups are overwritten within a further 35 days.

deadline.anchor: Termination or expiry of the Agreement

secondary_deadline.anchor: End of the 90-day deletion period (backup overwrite)

commitments.scope: Customer Personal Data, including backups

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will provide written certification of deletion upon Customer's written request.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must provide written certification of deletion when Customer asks in writing.

commitments.quote: If this DPA conflicts with the Agreement, this DPA controls as to the processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.summary: Where the DPA conflicts with the Agreement, the DPA controls on processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.scope: Processing of Customer Personal Data

commitments.quote: Customer Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Customer Data is encrypted with AES-256 at rest and with TLS 1.2 or higher in transit.
commitments.scope: Customer Data

commitments.quote: Access to production systems requires multi-factor authentication.
commitments.summary: Access to production systems requires multi-factor authentication.
commitments.scope: Production systems

commitments.quote: ExampleCo maintains a business continuity and disaster recovery plan and tests it at least annually.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo maintains a business continuity and disaster recovery plan and tests it at least once a year.

deadline.anchor: Annual test of the BC/DR plan

commitments.quote: Transfers of Customer Personal Data subject to EU or UK Data Protection Laws are made under the Standard Contractual Clauses, Module 2 or Module 3 as applicable.
commitments.summary: Transfers of Customer Personal Data subject to EU or UK law are made under the Standard Contractual Clauses, Module 2 or Module 3 as applicable.
commitments.scope: Customer Personal Data subject to EU or UK Data Protection Laws
